tags.violation_condition: A term and its parenthesised shortened form are introduced in a possessive construction.

when: The sentence defines a shortened form by giving the spelt-out term followed by the shortened form in parentheses.
This does not prohibit possessive shortened forms after they have been defined.
rules.why: G-4 combines the heading and its restatement; the check is limited to the defining construction.

anchor.quote: Don’t add an apostrophe to possessive pronouns.

covers.quote: A possessive pronoun doesn’t need an apostrophe
Don’t use an apostrophe for either type of pronoun.
Don’t confuse ‘it’s’ (the contraction of ‘it is’ or ‘it has’) with ‘its’ (showing that ‘it’ owns something).

covers.prefix: you need to use an apostrophe.
covers.quote: ‘Its’ is a determiner and doesn’t have an apostrophe.

tags.violation_condition: A possessive pronoun or possessive determiner contains an apostrophe, including it’s used with a possessive meaning.

when: Applies both to possessive pronouns standing in place of nouns and to possessive determiners before nouns.
An apostrophe in it’s is correct when it contracts it is or it has.
rules.why: G-2 combines the two possessive-pronoun categories; G-4 absorbs restatements and the possessive side of the its/it’s distinction.

anchor.quote: Don’t use an apostrophe for an Australian place name

covers.quote: Don’t use an apostrophe for Australian place names involving possessives.

tags.violation_condition: An Australian place name involving a possessive is written with a possessive apostrophe.

when: The place name is Australian and involves a possessive.
This does not address apostrophes serving other functions within place names.
rules.why: G-4 combines heading and body; the body limits the heading to possessive place names.

anchor.quote: Don’t use an apostrophe for a period of time

covers.quote: Noun phrases about plural time periods don’t need apostrophes because they’re usually descriptive, not possessive.
For many years, the Style Manual has recommended the simple rule of no apostrophe for either use.
When the time reference is in the singular, use an apostrophe to show that the noun is singular.

tags.violation_condition: A phrase about a plural time period contains a possessive apostrophe, whether the phrase is descriptive or shorthand for an of phrase.

when: Applies to plural time periods.
Covers descriptive uses and conversational shorthand for an of phrase.
Singular time references instead take an apostrophe under the possessive-ending rule.
rules.why: G-2 combines the two plural-time uses and records the singular exception; G-4 avoids a second rule for the body’s restatement.

anchor.quote: If you can divide ‘it’s’ into ‘it is’ or ‘it has’, then you need to use an apostrophe.

covers.quote: Don’t confuse ‘it’s’ (the contraction of ‘it is’ or ‘it has’) with ‘its’ (showing that ‘it’ owns something).

tags.violation_condition: Its is written without an apostrophe where it is intended as the contraction of it is or it has.

when: The intended expansion is it is or it has.
Possessive its has no apostrophe and is covered by the possessive-pronoun rule.
rules.why: G-4 selects the explicit test rather than the descriptive contraction heading; the possessive error is checked separately.

anchor.quote: Don’t use an apostrophe to make a noun plural

covers.quote: Don’t use them in descriptive phrases or to make nouns and shortened forms plural.
Add ‘s’ to make a plural shortened form – not apostrophe and ‘s’
Don’t write an apostrophe before the ‘s’. The same rule applies when making nouns plural.
No apostrophe is needed for the plural form of a noun.
covers.suffix: This type of error is known as

covers.quote: Don’t use an apostrophe for nouns and noun phrases formed by pluralising (and sometimes hyphenating) words that aren’t usually nouns.
The Style Manual follows the style for pluralising nouns – no apostrophe.
covers.suffix: We also prefer to use the minim

covers.quote: They are exceptions to the rule of not using an apostrophe for the plural form of a noun.

tags.violation_condition: An apostrophe is inserted to form a plural noun, shortened form, number, or nominalised word or phrase.

when: Includes plural shortened forms, multi-digit numbers and words or phrases that are not usually nouns.
An apostrophe already needed within a contraction is not a plural-forming apostrophe.
Plurals of single letters and single-digit numbers are exceptions: they require an apostrophe before s.
Possessive apostrophes are not plural-forming apostrophes.
rules.why: G-2 combines the kinds of plural receiving the same prohibition; G-4 absorbs restatements. Single-letter and single-digit plurals are excluded.

anchor.quote: Use an apostrophe before the ‘s’ for plurals of single letters and single-digit numbers.
anchor.suffix: They are exceptions to the rule

tags.violation_condition: A plural of a single letter or single-digit number is written without an apostrophe before its plural s.

when: The pluralised item is one letter or one single-digit number.
This is the stated exception to the general prohibition on plural-forming apostrophes.
rules.why: G-2 combines letters and single digits; this positive requirement checks an omission excluded from the general plural-apostrophe prohibition.

anchor.quote: Don’t italicise these plurals
anchor.suffix: or place them in quotation mark

tags.violation_condition: A plural of a single letter or single-digit number is italicised.

when: Applies to plurals of single letters and single-digit numbers.
rules.why: Italicisation is a distinct text-formatting finding from quotation marks or apostrophe formation.

anchor.quote: Don’t italicise these plurals or place them in quotation marks.

tags.violation_condition: A plural of a single letter or single-digit number is enclosed in quotation marks.

when: Applies to plurals of single letters and single-digit numbers.
The required apostrophe before plural s is not a pair of enclosing quotation marks.
rules.why: The sentence contains two independently flaggable prohibitions; this item checks quotation marks only.

anchor.quote: Use an apostrophe if the organisation does.

covers.quote: An apostrophe can form part of the official name of an organisation (or entity).
covers.suffix: Use an apostrophe if the organi

tags.violation_condition: An organisation or entity’s official name is written without an apostrophe that the organisation uses in its name.

when: The apostrophe forms part of the organisation or entity’s official name.
Official name usage takes precedence over a general descriptive-phrase analysis.
rules.why: The body gives an actionable naming requirement; G-5 excludes the separate instruction to research the name.
